patterns.label: Lexical Form
patterns.explain: The vav conjunction takes its lexical form, וְ, before a consonant that has a full vowel, except before the labials פ, מ and ב.

patterns.label: Labial / Simple Vocal Sheva
patterns.explain: Before a labial consonant (פ, מ, ב) or before a consonant with a simple vocal sheva, the vav becomes a šureq: וּ.

patterns.label: Compound Sheva
patterns.explain: Before a compound sheva, the vav takes the short vowel that matches the ḥāṭef (pataḥ, segol or qameṣ-ḥaṭuf), and usually has a meteg.

patterns.label: יְ
patterns.explain: Before a noun that begins with יְ, the vav takes a ḥireq and the yod loses its sheva: וִי.

patterns.label: Tone Syllable
patterns.explain: Before a tone syllable, or before a monosyllabic word, the vav takes a qameṣ: וָ.

patterns.label: Vav Consecutive
patterns.explain: This is a vav consecutive. The vav takes a qameṣ because compensatory lengthening occurs (before the א of a first-person imperfect).

patterns.label: Vav Consecutive
patterns.explain: This is a vav consecutive. The vav takes pataḥ (וַ) because the first consonant of the verb is a guttural that cannot take the dagesh (implicit doubling).

patterns.label: Vav Consecutive
patterns.explain: This is a vav consecutive. The vav takes pataḥ (וַ) and the dagesh forte is lost before a SQNMLVY consonant with a vocal sheva.

patterns.label: Vav Consecutive
patterns.explain: This is a vav consecutive. The vav takes pataḥ and a dagesh forte follows in the first letter of the converted imperfect verb (וַּ).

patterns.label: Divine Name
patterns.explain: Before the divine name יהוה the vav takes pataḥ (וַ), and before the divine name אֱלֹהִים it takes ṣere (וֵ).
